title: Create in me a clean heart (Psalm 51)
hook: David's prayer after his great wrong: a broken heart you won't despise

segments.voice: Yesterday, a river in a city that had none, and your line, found very much.

The prophet Nathan walks into the palace with a story about two men in one town. One rich, with flocks and herds. One poor, with a single little ewe lamb he raised with his own children, that ate from his plate and slept in his arms. A guest arrives, and instead of taking from his own flocks, the rich man takes the poor man's lamb and serves it for dinner. King David is furious. That man deserves to die, he says. And Nathan answers with four words: "Thou art the man." David has taken Bathsheba, another man's wife, and arranged for her husband Uriah to die in battle. The heading of today's psalm places it right here, in the silence after those four words.
screen: `ONE LITTLE EWE LAMB.` → `THOU ART THE MAN.` → `THE SILENCE AFTER.`

segments.voice: Psalm fifty-one begins, in the King James Bible: "Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness." No excuses. He asks to be washed, thoroughly, and cleansed. Then verse ten: "Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me." Create. In Hebrew it's bara, the same verb as the first line of the Bible, in the beginning God created. In its usual form, the Bible uses it only with God as the one doing it. So David isn't asking for a stain remover. He's asking God to do for his heart what God did for the world: make something new where there was only chaos. Sacrifices and offerings, he says, aren't what God is after. "The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise." Contrite means crushed, ground down. The thing you'd expect God to turn away from, the wreckage, is the one thing he won't refuse. Readers differ on whether the headings were part of the psalms from the start; tradition hears this one as David's own. In Latin it's called the Miserere, from its first word. Catholics, Orthodox, Anglicans and Lutherans pray it in Lent and on Ash Wednesday, and the daily prayer of some churches opens each morning with its verse fifteen: O Lord, open thou my lips.
screen: `HAVE MERCY. NO EXCUSES.` · `CREATE: THE VERB OF GENESIS 1` · `NOT SCRUBBED. MADE NEW.` · `A BROKEN HEART, NOT DESPISED` · then, large: `CREATE IN ME A CLEAN HEART, O GOD.`

segments.voice: Think of one place where you keep cleaning up the same mess, the same sharp tone, the same apology, and instead of scrubbing at it again, picture one concrete scene of a new start: what you'd say, what you'd do first. If you pray, say verse ten slowly: create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me. If you don't, simply hold the picture.
Bara. Hebrew for create, the same verb as in the beginning God created: what David asks for his own heart, not scrubbed clean, but made new.
Your line: a clean heart. Asked for with no excuses at all. That's four hundred twenty-four.

howItsDone: Psalm 51 is a prayer of repentance across the churches: Catholics, Orthodox, Anglicans and Lutherans pray it in Lent and on Ash Wednesday, and some Christians pray verse 10 before confession or at the start of the day.

options: say, I have sinned against the LORD.

fork.reveal: David says, "I have sinned against the LORD" (2 Samuel 12:13). no defense. Psalm 51's heading places the psalm right after this moment.

original.note: Hebrew: a clean heart. tahor is the word for clean, pure, fit to come near God.

trapdoor: what you thought: a prayer to feel a bit better about yourself.

what a scholar hears: bara, create, the verb of Genesis 1:1, which in its usual form the Bible uses only with God as the one creating.

psalms of turning back to God after sin

chat.says: In Psalm 51, why does David ask God to create a clean heart, not just wash it?
options: Create is bara, God's verb from Genesis: he's asking to be made new, not just scrubbed.
He thinks enough animal offerings at the temple will wash it clean, if he gives plenty.
He's explaining why what he did was different, so God will see it wasn't his fault.
chat.meaning: Bara, create, is the verb of in the beginning God created. David asks God to make something new in him, not just clean up.

Nathan.meaning: a prophet at King David's court

Bathsheba.meaning: Uriah's wife, whom King David took

Uriah.meaning: Bathsheba's husband, a soldier sent to die in battle

Miserere.meaning: Latin name for Psalm 51, from its first word: have mercy

Ash Wednesday.meaning: the day Lent begins, a season of turning back to God
